title: The Stockade
body: The Stockade is Stormwind's prison, hidden beneath the canal district, where thieves, agitators and killers are held. The guards no longer hold it. The Defias among the inmates rose in revolt and drove them out, and prisoners in red bandanas roam free through the cell blocks. The warden, pacing outside the gate, cannot understand how his prison was lost so suddenly, and is sure someone helped.

parts.body: The bandanas are torn from the prison's wool blankets. Nikova Raskol's grandson Mac, a guard only fourteen years old, scolded the prisoners for it, and they stabbed him in the back.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/The_Stockade, original World of Warcraft community site text (a high-security prison complex hidden beneath the canal district of Stormwind; its inmates; a prisoner-led revolt, the guards driven out); Geography: entrance on the northernmost section of the canal surrounding the Mage Quarter

parts.body: Darkshire sentenced Dextren Ward to die for selling Duskwood's dead to the necromancer Morbent Fel. The House of Nobles claimed him as Stormwind's prisoner instead, and he sits here still.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/The_Stockade, original World of Warcraft community site text (a high-security prison complex hidden beneath the canal district of Stormwind; its inmates; a prisoner-led revolt, the guards driven out); Geography: entrance on the northernmost section of the canal surrounding the Mage Quarter

parts.body: Kam Deepfury, the Dark Iron who planned the attack on Thandol Span, is held here for political reasons rather than executed.

title: Targorr the Dread
body: Targorr the Dread was supreme executioner to Gath'Ilzogg, warlord of the Blackrock Clan, and tortured captured defenders of the kingdom at his whim. Taken at last, he was locked in the Stockade under sentence of death, but one of the nobles in the capital put a hold on his execution, and in Lakeshire they are sure of foul play.

title: Bazil Thredd
body: Bazil Thredd was Edwin VanCleef's lieutenant in the Stonemasons' Guild and followed him out of Stormwind, until he was caught and locked in the Stockade. For years he had no visitors, and the warden took him for a man the Brotherhood had abandoned. The riot proved otherwise: it is Thredd's.

parts.body: A few months before the riot a quiet man began to visit Thredd once or twice a week, his papers in order, his name given as Maelik.
